meta.title: Cloud Security Baseline Generator
meta.note: A prioritized hardening baseline grounded in the CIS Foundations Benchmarks. Guidance to adapt, not an audit or a substitute for provider documentation.

sources.name: CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark

workloads.name: SaaS product
workloads.hint: A customer-facing application you build and run.

workloads.name: Corporate IT
workloads.hint: Employee identity, email, and internal systems.

workloads.name: Data platform
workloads.hint: Analytics or data lake holding large regulated datasets.

controls.title: Enable hardware or virtual MFA on the AWS account root user
controls.rationale: The root user can do anything in the account and cannot be constrained by IAM policy. Without MFA, a single leaked root password gives an attacker total control of the account.

controls.title: Delete root user access keys and avoid using root for daily tasks
controls.rationale: Long-lived root access keys grant programmatic god-mode access that bypasses per-user auditing. If they leak, the entire account is compromised with no way to scope the damage.

controls.title: Set a strong IAM account password policy (length, complexity, reuse limits)
controls.rationale: A weak password policy lets users pick guessable credentials that are easy to brute force or spray. Enforcing minimum length and reuse prevention raises the bar for credential attacks.

controls.title: Require MFA for all IAM users and IAM Identity Center human logins
controls.rationale: Console passwords alone are frequently phished or reused across sites. Enforcing MFA on every human login blocks the large majority of credential-based account takeovers.

controls.title: Centralize human access via IAM Identity Center with federated SSO
controls.rationale: Managing standalone IAM users per account leads to orphaned credentials and inconsistent offboarding. IAM Identity Center provides central, temporary, role-based access tied to your identity provider.

controls.title: Use IAM roles over long-lived keys and rotate or retire stale credentials
controls.rationale: Long-lived access keys are a top cause of cloud breaches when they leak in code or logs. Preferring short-lived role credentials and pruning unused keys shrinks the credential attack surface.

controls.title: Enable a multi-region CloudTrail trail with log file validation
controls.rationale: CloudTrail is the authoritative record of API activity across the account; without it you cannot investigate incidents or prove compliance. Multi-region coverage and log validation prevent blind spots and tampering.

controls.title: Enable AWS Config in all regions to record resource configuration history
controls.rationale: AWS Config tracks how resources are configured and how they change over time, which is essential for drift detection and audit evidence. Without it you cannot show whether controls stayed in place.

controls.title: Store logs in a separate, restricted archive made immutable with S3 Object Lock and versioning
controls.rationale: Send logs to a dedicated, tightly restricted account or bucket and make them immutable with S3 Object Lock (compliance mode) plus versioning, so an attacker who gains access cannot erase the evidence of their activity.

controls.title: Enable Amazon GuardDuty threat detection in every active region
controls.rationale: GuardDuty continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC flow, and DNS logs to surface compromised credentials, crypto mining, and reconnaissance. Without it, malicious activity often goes unnoticed for weeks.

controls.title: Block 0.0.0.0/0 ingress to SSH, RDP, and database ports in security groups
controls.rationale: Security groups open to the entire internet on admin or database ports are scanned and attacked within minutes. Restricting ingress to known ranges or bastions removes an easy entry point.

controls.title: Restrict the default security group of every VPC to deny all traffic
controls.rationale: Resources launched without an explicit security group inherit the default one, which can silently allow unintended access. Locking the default group down prevents accidental exposure.

controls.title: Enable VPC Flow Logs on all VPCs and ship them to central storage
controls.rationale: Flow logs capture accepted and rejected network traffic, which is critical for detecting exfiltration and lateral movement. Without them, network-layer incidents cannot be reconstructed.

controls.title: Place databases and internal workloads in private subnets behind NAT
controls.rationale: Backend systems in public subnets are directly reachable from the internet, expanding the attack surface. Isolating them in private subnets forces traffic through controlled gateways and load balancers.

controls.title: Enforce IMDSv2 (token-required) on all EC2 instances and launch templates
controls.rationale: IMDSv1 lets SSRF flaws in an application steal instance role credentials from the metadata endpoint. Requiring IMDSv2 session tokens closes this common credential theft path.

controls.title: Manage OS patching and access with Systems Manager instead of SSH keys
controls.rationale: Unpatched instances and static SSH keys are frequent breach vectors. Systems Manager Patch Manager keeps hosts current and Session Manager provides audited, keyless access.

controls.title: Enable ECR image scanning and encrypt container repositories
controls.rationale: Container images often ship with known vulnerable packages that reach production unnoticed. Enabling ECR scan on push surfaces critical CVEs before they are deployed.

controls.title: Turn on S3 Block Public Access at the account and bucket level
controls.rationale: Misconfigured S3 buckets are one of the most common causes of large data leaks. Account-level Block Public Access prevents any bucket or object from being made public by mistake.

controls.title: Enforce default encryption at rest with KMS on S3, EBS, and RDS
controls.rationale: Unencrypted volumes and buckets expose regulated data if snapshots, disks, or backups are accessed. KMS-managed encryption with key policies protects data and supports auditable key control.

controls.title: Configure AWS Backup with encrypted, immutable copies and tested restores
controls.rationale: Ransomware and accidental deletion can destroy primary data if backups are missing or writable. Centralized, immutable backups with periodic restore tests ensure recoverability.

controls.title: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all Entra ID Global Administrators
controls.rationale: Global Administrator accounts control the entire tenant; without MFA a single stolen credential grants full takeover of identities, subscriptions, and data.

controls.title: Require MFA for all Entra ID users via Conditional Access
controls.rationale: Standard user accounts are the most common initial access vector; requiring MFA for every sign-in blocks password spray and credential replay attacks.

controls.title: Block legacy authentication protocols with a Conditional Access policy
controls.rationale: Legacy protocols (POP, IMAP, SMTP, older Office clients) cannot enforce MFA, so attackers use them to bypass modern controls. Blocking them closes that gap.

controls.title: Limit Global Administrators to fewer than five dedicated accounts
controls.rationale: Every extra Global Administrator widens the tenant attack surface; keeping the count low and using purpose-built accounts reduces standing high-privilege exposure.

controls.title: Enable Entra ID PIM just-in-time activation for privileged roles
controls.rationale: Privileged Identity Management removes standing admin access by requiring time-bound, approved activation; this shrinks the window an attacker can abuse elevated roles.

controls.title: Enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud paid plans across all resource types
controls.rationale: Defender for Cloud provides threat detection and security posture alerts; leaving it on the free tier means server, storage, and database intrusions go undetected.

controls.title: Route diagnostic settings and Activity Log to a Log Analytics workspace
controls.rationale: Centralized diagnostic and Activity Log collection in Azure Monitor is required for investigation and correlation; without it, incident evidence is scattered or lost.

controls.title: Retain Activity Log data for at least 365 days
controls.rationale: Long retention supports forensic timelines and compliance audits; short retention erases the evidence needed to reconstruct an incident after slow-moving compromise.

controls.title: Deny inbound RDP and SSH from the Internet in all NSG rules
controls.rationale: Management ports open to the Internet are continuously scanned and brute forced; restricting 3389 and 22 to bastion or trusted ranges removes a top ransomware entry path.

controls.title: Enable NSG flow logs and review overly permissive rules
controls.rationale: Flow logs give visibility into allowed and denied traffic; combined with regular rule review they catch any-any exposures before attackers exploit them.

controls.title: Use Private Endpoints for PaaS storage, databases, and Key Vault
controls.rationale: Private Endpoints keep traffic to managed services on the Azure backbone and off public IPs, reducing data exfiltration and public exposure of sensitive stores.

controls.title: Enable Defender for Servers with endpoint protection on all VMs
controls.rationale: Defender for Servers adds EDR, vulnerability assessment, and behavioral alerts to virtual machines; without it, compromised hosts run malware undetected.

controls.title: Enable Azure Update Manager for automated OS patching of VMs
controls.rationale: Unpatched operating systems are a leading exploitation vector; centralized update management ensures critical CVEs are remediated on a predictable schedule.

controls.title: Enable encryption at host or Azure Disk Encryption on all VM disks
controls.rationale: Encrypting OS and data disks protects information at rest if underlying storage is accessed; unencrypted disks risk data disclosure during theft or misconfiguration.

controls.title: Disable public blob access on all storage accounts
controls.rationale: Publicly accessible storage accounts and containers are a frequent cause of mass data leaks; disabling public access ensures data is reachable only via authorized paths.

controls.title: Require secure transfer and TLS 1.2 minimum on storage accounts
controls.rationale: Enforcing HTTPS and a modern TLS floor prevents data from traversing the network in cleartext or over weak ciphers vulnerable to interception.

controls.title: Enable Key Vault soft-delete and purge protection
controls.rationale: Purge protection stops attackers or accidental actions from permanently destroying keys and secrets; without it, deleted cryptographic material can be lost irrecoverably.

controls.title: Enforce 2-Step Verification (2SV/MFA) for all Cloud Identity and Workspace users
controls.rationale: Passwords alone are routinely phished or reused; enforcing 2SV org-wide stops the vast majority of account takeovers. Without it, one stolen credential can compromise the whole GCP organization.

controls.title: Avoid primitive Owner and Editor roles; use predefined or custom least-privilege roles
controls.rationale: Primitive roles (Owner, Editor) grant broad, project-wide access that ignores least privilege and is hard to audit. Overuse means a single compromised principal can read, modify, or destroy nearly everything in the project.

controls.title: Restrict service account key creation and rotate or eliminate user-managed keys
controls.rationale: Long-lived, user-managed service account keys are a common credential-leak vector and rarely rotated. Enforce the iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation org policy and prefer Workload Identity Federation so leaked keys cannot grant standing access.

controls.title: Use Cloud Identity or SSO federation and restrict access to the corporate domain
controls.rationale: Centralizing users in Cloud Identity with SSO lets you enforce provisioning, deprovisioning, and session policy from one place. The Domain Restricted Sharing org policy blocks IAM grants to outside accounts, preventing accidental external access.

controls.title: Separate duties for key and IAM admin roles; avoid single-person control of secrets
controls.rationale: One principal holding both administration and approval powers (for example Cloud KMS admin plus encrypter/decrypter) can act unchecked. Splitting these roles enforces separation of duties and limits insider or takeover blast radius.

controls.title: Enable Cloud Audit Logs including Data Access logs across all services
controls.rationale: Admin Activity logs are on by default, but Data Access logs (who read or wrote data) must be enabled explicitly. Without them you cannot reconstruct a breach or prove access during an audit.

controls.title: Configure an org-level log sink to a retained, access-controlled bucket
controls.rationale: A centralized aggregated export sink to Cloud Storage or a Log bucket preserves logs beyond default retention and beyond a compromised project. Apply retention locks and tight IAM so attackers cannot delete or tamper with the trail.

controls.title: Enable Security Command Center and log-based metric alerts on key changes
controls.rationale: Security Command Center surfaces misconfigurations and threats across the org, and log-based metric alerts catch high-risk events (IAM changes, firewall edits, VPC route changes) in near real time. Without alerting, dangerous changes go unnoticed until impact.

controls.title: Delete the default VPC network and remove overly permissive default firewall rules
controls.rationale: The auto-created default network ships with permissive firewall rules (for example allow-internal and open ICMP) that violate least privilege. Removing it forces intentional, segmented network design instead of accidental exposure.

controls.title: Block 0.0.0.0/0 ingress to SSH (22) and RDP (3389); use IAP for admin access
controls.rationale: Firewall rules opening SSH or RDP to the entire internet invite brute-force and exploitation of exposed management ports. Restrict source ranges and route admin access through Identity-Aware Proxy so no port is publicly reachable.

controls.title: Enable VPC Flow Logs and Private Google Access on production subnets
controls.rationale: VPC Flow Logs give the network telemetry needed for intrusion detection, forensics, and traffic review. Private Google Access lets instances reach Google APIs without public IPs, shrinking the internet-facing attack surface.

controls.title: Enable Shielded VM (Secure Boot, vTPM, integrity monitoring) on Compute instances
controls.rationale: Shielded VM defends against boot- and kernel-level rootkits and verifies instance integrity at startup. Without it, a compromised boot chain can persist undetected beneath the operating system.

controls.title: Harden GKE with private clusters, Binary Authorization, and Workload Identity
controls.rationale: Private clusters remove public control-plane and node exposure, Binary Authorization blocks unsigned or untrusted images, and Workload Identity replaces node service account keys. Together they stop untrusted code and lateral movement in the cluster.

controls.title: Use VM Manager OS patch management to remediate vulnerabilities on a schedule
controls.rationale: Unpatched operating systems are among the most exploited entry points. VM Manager patch deployments and compliance reporting keep Compute Engine fleets current and give evidence of a managed patch cadence.

controls.title: Block public GCS buckets and enforce uniform bucket-level access org-wide
controls.rationale: Public or ACL-managed buckets are a leading cause of cloud data leaks. Public Access Prevention plus uniform bucket-level access disable anonymous access and fine-grained ACLs so permissions are governed consistently by IAM.

controls.title: Encrypt sensitive GCS, BigQuery, and disks with customer-managed keys (CMEK) in Cloud KMS
controls.rationale: CMEK gives you control over key rotation, access, and revocation beyond Google-managed defaults, which many regulated frameworks expect. Revoking or disabling a key can cut off access to data during an incident.

controls.title: Restrict BigQuery dataset access and prevent datasets shared to allAuthenticatedUsers
controls.rationale: Datasets granted to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers expose regulated analytics data broadly. Scope dataset and table IAM to specific principals and use authorized views so sensitive columns are not overshared.
